collect.bio: Raphaël Glucksmann (born 15 October 1979) is a French essayist, documentary filmmaker and politician, son of philosopher André Glucksmann. He co-founded Place publique in 2018 and has been a Member of the European Parliament (S&D group) since 2019, leading the PS-Place publique list in 2019 (6.2%) and 2024 (13.83%, third place). He has co-led Place publique with Aurore Lalucq since December 2022. On 23 August 2026 he announced his candidacy in the Socialist Party primary for the 2027 presidential election.

Recent coverage across outlets (Politico, Le Monde, Mediapart, Le Parisien, Ouest-France, Sud Ouest, CNews) reported two episodes: a campaign memo on 'target audiences' leaked by Politico on 12 May 2026, which he called stolen and of no political value, and a video recorded on 17 September 2026 and released by Le Média on 2 October, in which he insulted Mélenchon and Le Pen and said Ségolène Royal had done 'la danse du ventre' for Macron; he apologised to Royal for 'inelegant' remarks during the 4 October primary debate.

verify.sources_note: Sources consulted: the French and English Wikipedia articles on Glucksmann (via WebFetch summaries), plus Bing News result listings used to confirm the dates of his candidacy announcement (TF1, 23 August 2026; reported by BFMTV, TF1 Info, Valeurs actuelles, Le Temps), the May 2026 memo leak (20 Minuten, citing Politico), and the October 2026 video and apology (Le Parisien, Ouest-France, Sud Ouest, CNews). The WebSearch budget was exhausted, and no primary sources (programme, roll-call votes) were verified. The legal list is empty because Wikipedia does not mention any personal judicial case, complaint or investigation, but no dedicated court or press check was possible. Reversals and traits stay empty because the two-source, different-lean rule could not be met. Possible reversal candidates that were not documented to the required standard: his stance on LFI (he ran with the Nouveau Front populaire in 2024, then called for the left to distance itself from LFI). Wikipedia notes policy positions: very cautious use of the word 'genocide' about Gaza while denouncing a 'massacre' and the blockade, rejection of an alliance with LFI, leaving Dublin III, criticism of the 2024 EU Migration and Asylum Pact, support for wealth taxation, and support for Ukraine's EU integration. A rerun with a higher search budget is recommended.
